groups.title: Syrup (415702ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation.
groups.usage: Adults: at the start of treatment, take 30 mL once a day, with breakfast or with dinner. In most patients, after a few days the maintenance dose is 15 mL, taken 1 time in 1 day. In children the average dose is 0.375 mL per kg of body weight in 1 day: ages 1 to 6 years, 3.75 to 7.5 mL a day; ages 6 to 12 years, 7.5 to 15 mL a day; ages 12 to 16 years, 15 to 30 mL a day. Because the response differs from person to person, the dose for a person with constipation must be adjusted to the amount needed for 1 bowel movement a day. This medicine may be mixed with a hot or cold drink, cereal or pudding.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to this medicine, intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), abdominal pain or bleeding of unknown cause, faecal impaction, galactosaemia, an incision of the ileum or rectum, inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease and the like) or a colostomy, or if you are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, if the user is an infant, a young child or an older person, if the user is debilitated, or if there is fluid and electrolyte imbalance or chronic constipation.

It is advisable to maintain an adequate fluid intake every day. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking this medicine and consult a pharmacist.

Consult a pharmacist before use with thiazide diuretics, corticosteroids, carbenoxolone, amphotericin B, cardiac glycosides, or alpha-glucosidase inhibitors (acarbose, voglibose).

groups.title: Eye Drops (D49001COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for dryness of the eye (discomfort, stinging pain, irritation) or eye fatigue caused by wind, smoke, air pollution, dust, dry heat, air conditioning, air travel or prolonged computer use.
groups.usage: When needed, instil 1 drop into each eye, 1 or more times a day as required. After instillation, discard the remaining solution and the container.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe eye pain, if you have ever had an allergic reaction to an eye medicine (for example redness of the eye, itching, swelling, rash or reddening), or if you have glaucoma.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only. Wash your hands thoroughly before use. To prevent contamination, do not share it with others. If symptoms become worse, or if they last for 3 days or more, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Plaster (C03400CPL)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of pain and inflammation of bruises, stiff shoulder and rheumatic pain.
groups.usage: Clean the affected area and let it dry, then apply 1 patch, 1 time in 1 day. If necessary, hold it in place with a bandage or adhesive plaster.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine on eczema, on dermatitis caused by lacquer or similar plants, or on broken skin.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had an allergy to a medicine or a cosmetic, if you have an allergic constitution, if the area is severely wet or eroded, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if you are breast-feeding.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. For external use only. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 days of use, stop using it and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Eye Drops (332600COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the temporary relief of eye irritation and redness of the eye.
groups.usage: Instil 1 to 2 drops into the eye, 4 times in 1 day. After instillation, discard the remaining solution and the container immediately (single-use eye drops only).
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or if you have closed-angle glaucoma.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child, if you have a severe cardiovascular disease such as cardiac arrhythmia, if you have high blood pressure that is not well controlled, or if you have diabetes with a possibility of diabetic ketoacidosis.

Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only. To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with others. After opening, use it once immediately and discard the remaining solution and the container at once (single-use eye drops only). If symptoms do not improve after 3 days or more of use, stop using it and consult a pharmacist.

Consult a pharmacist before use together with a monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitor.

groups.title: Eye Drops (228606COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the temporary relief of burning, irritation and discomfort caused by dry eye or by exposure to wind and sun, and for the prevention of eye irritation.
groups.usage: When needed, instil 1 to 2 drops into the affected eye, then discard the remaining solution and the container. If another eye drop is used at the same time, allow an interval of at least 15 minutes between them to avoid a dilution effect.
groups.caution:
For external use only.

Do not reuse after a single use; always discard the remaining solution and the container.

To avoid contamination, do not let the tip of the container touch any surface.

Do not use the solution if its colour has changed or if it has become cloudy.

Temporary blurring of vision may occur, so take care when driving or operating dangerous machinery until your vision is clear again.

groups.title: Ointment (A23900COM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for eczema, heat rash, itching of the skin, allergic skin disease, burns and frostbite.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area, 2 to 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine on chickenpox, athlete's foot, tinea or suppurating (pus-forming) areas, on mucous membranes such as the conjunctiva of the eye, or over wide areas of the face.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have ever had an allergy to a medicine or a cosmetic, if the affected area is extensive, severely wet or badly eroded, or if you are pregnant or may be pregnant.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Use this medicine externally only; do not take it by mouth.

groups.title: Eye Drops (A73600COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for eye fatigue, for supplementing tears (dryness of the eye), for discomfort while wearing hard or soft contact lenses, and for blurred or gritty eyes (for example when there is a lot of eye discharge).
groups.usage: Instil 1 to 2 drops per dose, 4 to 5 times in 1 day, increasing or decreasing the frequency appropriately according to symptoms. After instillation, discard the remaining solution and the container.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have severe eye pain, if you have ever had an allergic reaction to an eye medicine (redness of the eye, itching, swelling), or if you have glaucoma.

When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with others. After opening, use it once immediately and discard the remaining solution and the container at once. If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (172301ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for gastric and duodenal ulcer, oesophageal spasm, pyloric spasm, gastritis, enteritis, intestinal colic, spastic constipation, functional diarrhoea, cholecystitis, cholangitis, cholelithiasis (gallstones), biliary dyskinesia, sequelae after cholecystectomy, urinary stones, cystitis and dysmenorrhoea (menstrual pain).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 tablets (10 to 20 mg) per dose, 3 to 5 times in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, glaucoma, a functional narrowing of the gastrointestinal tract such as pyloric stenosis, paralytic or obstructive ileus, myasthenia gravis, megacolon, irregular tachycardia, severe heart disease, haemorrhagic colitis, or difficulty passing urine due to prostatic hyperplasia, or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have bacterial diarrhoea, congestive heart failure, arrhythmia, ulcerative colitis, hyperthyroidism, if you are in a high-temperature environment, if you have prostatic hyperplasia, or if you are an older person.

After taking this medicine, disturbance of visual accommodation and dizziness may occur, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine together with phenothiazine medicines, tricyclic or tetracyclic antidepressants, MAO inhibitors, antihistamines, antipsychotics, quinidine, amantadine, anticholinergic medicines such as disopyramide and other anticholinergics (tiotropium, ipratropium, atropine-like compounds), dopamine antagonists such as metoclopramide, or beta agonists.

groups.title: Oral Solution (D05901ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as adjunctive treatment for indigestion caused by impaired liver function.
groups.usage: Adults: take 2 to 3 bottles (40 to 60 mL) in 1 day. Children: take 1 bottle (20 mL) in 1 day. Take it before meals with a glass of water.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, severe hepatic failure (loss of liver function), obstruction of the bile duct, or myocardial infarction now or in the past.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have diabetes.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Take this medicine by mouth only. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Oral Suspension (105201ASS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for its antacid action and for the improvement of symptoms in gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis, excess stomach acid, heartburn, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain and acid eructation (sour belching).
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 1 to 1.5 g per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes to 1 hour after meals. If necessary, 1 further dose may be taken before bedtime.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, Alzheimer's disease, haemorrhoids, fluid retention (swelling), pregnancy toxaemia, diarrhoea, or undiagnosed gastrointestinal bleeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment, if you are physically weak, if you are on a diet low in phosphorus, if you have a disorder of digestion and absorption, if you are an older person, if you have signs of gastrointestinal bleeding such as vomiting of blood or black stools, or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take a tetracycline antibiotic while you are taking this medicine. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, an ulcer medicine, a digitalis preparation, chlorpromazine, lansoprazole, prednisolone, penicillin, a quinolone, an iron (Fe) salt preparation, or a salicylate.

groups.title: Cream (546600CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for fungal skin infections (tinea, cutaneous candidiasis, tinea versicolor) accompanied by clinical signs such as inflammation, itching and eczema.
groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area, 1 to 2 times in 1 day (in the morning, or in the morning and the evening).
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; on skin infections (tuberculosis, syphilis, herpes zoster, herpes simplex, chickenpox, vaccinia); on eczematous otitis externa with perforation of the eardrum; on ulcers (except Behcet's disease); on deep second-degree or more severe burns and frostbite; on perioral dermatitis, acne vulgaris, rosacea, syphilis, tuberculosis or skin vaccine reactions; on broken skin; or over wide areas (10 % or more of the body surface).

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, if the user is an infant or a young child, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to propylene glycol.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Use it externally only; do not take it by mouth. If it is used on the genital area together with latex contraceptives (condoms and vaginal suppositories), it may damage them and may reduce their safety and effectiveness.

groups.title: Syrup (180801ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for chronic constipation, constipation in infants and children, and constipation after childbirth.
groups.usage: For chronic constipation in adults: take 15 to 30 mL a day before breakfast for the first 2 to 3 days, then continue with 10 to 15 mL in 1 day. In severe cases up to 45 mL may be taken. Children aged 7 to 14 years: take 15 mL a day for the first 2 to 3 days, then continue with 10 mL a day. Young children aged 1 to 6 years: 5 to 10 mL a day. Infants under 12 months: 5 mL a day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease), gastrointestinal obstruction, abdominal pain of unknown cause, if you are on a low-galactose diet (galactosaemia), if you have perforation of the digestive tract or a risk of it, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, if the user is an infant, a young child or an older person, or if there is diabetes, fructose intolerance, fluid and electrolyte imbalance, acute gastritis or chronic constipation.

Consult a pharmacist if you are taking an alpha-glucosidase inhibitor such as acarbose, a broad-spectrum antibiotic, a diuretic, a corticoid, amphotericin B, a cardiac glycoside or an antacid.

groups.title: Tablet (185401ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for allergic rhinitis (sneezing, blocked nose, itching, burning of the eyes) and for chronic idiopathic urticaria (hives of unknown cause).
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet (10 mg), 1 time in 1 day. Children aged 6 to under 12 years: if body weight is 30 kg or more, take 1 tablet (10 mg) 1 time in 1 day; if body weight is 30 kg or less, take 1/2 tablet (5 mg) 1 time in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child under 6 years of age, if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have liver impairment or renal failure.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take it together with cimetidine, erythromycin, ketoconazole, quinidine, fluconazole, fluoxetine or other medicines that inhibit liver metabolism.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for calcium deficiency and other supplementation of calcium, for supplementation of vitamin D during pregnancy and breast-feeding, during growth and in old age, and for the prevention of poor development of bones and teeth and of rickets.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 to 2 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is an infant under 12 months of age, or if there is hypercalcaemia (an excess of calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease, kidney stones or severe renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the child gets a lot of sunlight and eats a normal diet, if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, if the user is a premature baby or a young child, if there is impaired heart or circulatory function, hypoproteinaemia, a history of kidney stones, or hypersensitivity now or in the past to Yellow No. 5.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids, fluoroquinolone antibiotics or levothyroxine. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with cardiac glycosides, anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

groups.title: Syrup (A31500ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain) and for the relief of the various symptoms of hay fever (pollen allergic rhinitis) and of other upper respiratory tract allergies (runny nose, sneezing, itching of the eyes, nose and throat, and watering eyes).
groups.usage: Adolescents and adults aged 12 years and older: take 1 sachet every 4 to 6 hours when needed. Do not take more than 4 sachets in 24 hours. Dissolve 1 sachet in about 250 mL of hot water that is not boiling and drink it within 10 to 15 minutes.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had, or have a history of, an asthma attack caused by another antipyretic analgesic (non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic) or by a cold medicine; if you have severe cardiac insufficiency, high blood pressure, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, diabetes, epilepsy or glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; if you have phaeochromocytoma; if you are an older person with confusion; or if you have a hereditary problem such as fructose intolerance, glucose-galactose malabsorption or sucrase deficiency.

Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinson medicines and the like), antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, antihistamines, other sympathomimetic medicines, tricyclic antidepressants, antihypertensive medicines (vasodilators, beta blockers, debrisoquine, guanethidine, reserpine, methyldopa and the like), barbiturates, metoclopramide, domperidone, cholestyramine, warfarin, coumarin anticoagulants, chloramphenicol, zidovudine, probenecid, digoxin and other cardiac glycosides, or ergot alkaloids (ergotamine, methysergide).

groups.title: Eye Drops (D64600COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for discomfort while wearing soft or hard contact lenses, for supplementing tears (dryness of the eye), for eye fatigue and for blurred eyes (when there is a lot of eye discharge).
groups.usage: Instil 2 to 3 drops per dose, 5 to 6 times in 1 day. After instillation, discard the remaining solution and the container immediately (single-use products only).
groups.caution:
Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have ever had an allergic reaction to a medicine, if you have an allergic constitution, if you have glaucoma, or if you have severe eye pain.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Do not use it if the solution is cloudy. Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only. At first use, discard the first 1 to 2 drops without instilling them. If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Do not share it with other people. For a single-use product, use it only once after opening and discard the remaining solution and the container immediately.

If rash, reddening (flushing of the skin), itching, redness of the eye, itching or swelling of the eye occurs, or if a wearer of hard contact lenses has a lot of discharge such as eye mucus or the lenses become cloudy, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you are breast-feeding, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have gastric ulcer, severe kidney impairment, hepatic failure or severe liver disease, impaired bronchial motility with copious secretions, if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if you are an older person.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking an antibiotic such as erythromycin, cefalexin, cefuroxime, amoxicillin, doxycycline or oxytetracycline.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: severe skin disorders such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) or toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); non-specific influenza-like symptoms (fever, body aches, rhinitis, cough and sore throat); diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain; occasionally headache, rash, difficulty breathing, transient chills; or hypersensitivity reactions such as urticaria, bronchospasm, angioedema, itching or signs of anaphylactic shock.

groups.title: Syrup (123841ASY)

groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child under 2 years of age, or if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, if you are an older person, if you have liver impairment or heart impairment, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to caramel.

Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an antibiotic or with a syrup containing trimetoquinol hydrochloride.

groups.title: Tablet (104601ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the improvement of symptoms that accompany abnormal vitamin D metabolism in chronic renal failure, hypoparathyroidism and vitamin D-resistant rickets and osteomalacia (hypocalcaemia, tetany, bone pain, bone lesions and the like), and for osteoporosis.
groups.usage: For chronic renal failure and osteoporosis in adults: take 1 to 2 tablets (0.5 to 1 microgram) by mouth, 1 time in 1 day. For hypoparathyroidism and other diseases caused by abnormal vitamin D metabolism in adults: take 2 to 8 tablets (1 to 4 micrograms) by mouth, 1 time in 1 day. For osteoporosis in children: take 0.01 to 0.03 micrograms per kg of body weight by mouth, 1 time in 1 day. For other diseases in children: take 0.05 to 0.1 micrograms per kg of body weight by mouth, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, hypercalcaemia, hyperphosphataemia, hypermagnesaemia, a Ca x P product greater than 3.7 (mmol/L)2, alkalaemia with a blood pH above 7.44 (milk-alkali syndrome, Burnett's syndrome), or signs of vitamin D toxicity.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, if the user is a child or an older person, if you have a history of kidney stones, or if you have sarcoidosis.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Follow the instructions you have been given about calcium intake from the diet or from supplements.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take magnesium-containing preparations, vitamin D and its derivatives, calcium-containing preparations or thiazide diuretics. Consult a pharmacist if you are taking digitalis, a resin such as cholestyramine, the laxative mineral oil, phenytoin, glucocorticoids, colestipol, sucralfate, an antacid with a high aluminium content, oestrogens (ethinylestradiol, norethisterone), barbiturates or antiepileptic medicines.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: occasionally gastrointestinal disorders such as loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, constipation or stomach pain, stomach discomfort, abdominal distension, indigestion; rarely thirst or an abnormal sensation in the mouth; excessive drinking and thirst, pancreatitis, a metallic taste, cramp of the leg muscles, headache, a heavy head, insomnia, irritability, weakness, lassitude, dizziness, numbness, drowsiness, heartburn, stiff shoulder, senile hearing loss, tinnitus (ringing in the ears), decline of memory and recall, overt psychosis, other disturbance of consciousness, back pain, a mild rise in blood pressure; rarely palpitations, other cardiac arrhythmia, acute renal failure, raised BUN and creatinine (reduced kidney function), kidney stones, other nephrocalcinosis, liver function disorder, jaundice, itching, rash, a feeling of heat, conjunctival congestion, other conjunctivitis, corneal calcification, sensitivity to light, calcification around the joints (bone formation), other bone pain, hoarseness, oedema (swelling), other weight loss, difficulty passing urine, polyuria (excessive urine), night-time urination, ectopic calcification, muscle pain, runny nose, high fever, reduced libido, protein in the urine or high blood cholesterol.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E12700ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, sputum, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is an infant under 3 months of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is an infant or child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is an infant aged 3 months or older and under 2 years, or a young child; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not take it continuously for a long period. Do not drink alcohol while taking it. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after about 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinson medicines and the like), antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines). Consult a pharmacist if you are taking a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, a barbiturate, a tricyclic antidepressant or alcohol.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema (swelling), difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia; signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters); asthma; general lassitude; jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes); cough with breathlessness and difficulty breathing; fever; or signs of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like).

groups.title: Troche (A00401ATO)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of inflammation caused by pharyngitis, tonsillitis and stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth).
groups.usage: Adults: let 1 tablet (1.5 mg) dissolve slowly in the mouth 4 to 5 times in 1 day, without chewing it and without swallowing it. The amount may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine in infants and young children aged 3 years or younger.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have allergic contact eczema, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4.

Do not chew it and do not swallow it; let it dissolve slowly in the saliva and keep it in the mouth as long as possible so that it stays in the mouth for a long time.

If rash or a hypersensitivity reaction of the oral mucosa (urticaria, erosion, and rarely a burning sensation in the mouth and throat) occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist. High fever, headache and nausea may occur.

groups.title: Capsule (379302ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (40 mg as iron) per dose, 1 to 2 times in 1 day, avoiding mealtimes.
groups.caution:
An overdose in a child aged 6 years or younger can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is an infant under 12 months of age; or if you have haemochromatosis, haemosiderosis, impaired iron utilisation, anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency, anaemia due to bone marrow failure, haemolytic anaemia, iron overload, pernicious anaemia, iron deficiency anaemia caused by infection or a tumour, chronic pancreatitis or liver cirrhosis.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. For the best effect it is better to take it apart from meals.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics or antacids. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking an iron-containing preparation (an iron supplement, an MRI liver contrast agent and the like), an anti-aldosterone medicine, triamterene, a quinolone, penicillamine, neomycin, cholestyramine, pancreatic extract, vitamin E, a diphosphonate salt, thyroxine, a cefdinir preparation, or 200 mg or more of ascorbic acid (vitamin C). groups.title: Patch (A88115CPC)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as an aid when stopping smoking.
groups.usage: Adults: apply 1 patch 1 time in 1 day to a hairless part of the body (the buttock, the inner arm and the like), changing the site of application every day. Nicotinell TTS 30 is generally used for smokers of 20 or more cigarettes a day, and Nicotinell TTS 20 for smokers of up to 20 cigarettes a day. Nicotinell TTS 10 is used in the final stage to reduce nicotine replacement. A heavy smoker starts with Nicotinell TTS 30, then Nicotinell TTS 20, and finally Nicotinell TTS 10, each for 4 weeks. An ordinary smoker uses Nicotinell TTS 20 for 8 weeks and then Nicotinell TTS 10 for 4 weeks. Treatment must not exceed 3 months.
groups.caution:
If you continue to smoke while using this medicine, cardiovascular adverse effects of nicotine may occur more often and more markedly, so it should be used only by people who have stopped smoking completely.

Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; a chronic skin disease (psoriasis, chronic dermatitis, urticaria); a generalised skin disease; hypersensitivity dermatitis; unstable angina or worsening angina; myocardial infarction within the past 3 months; the late phase after an acute infarction; severe cardiac arrhythmia; systemic hypertension; peripheral vascular disease; cerebrovascular disease (acute stroke, cerebrovascular abnormality); if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; if the user is a child or adolescent under 18 years of age; or if the user is a non-smoker or an occasional smoker.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have gastritis, peptic ulcer, occlusive arterial disease, stable angina, heart failure, decompensated heart failure, myocardial infarction, cardiac arrhythmia, vasospasm, uncontrolled high blood pressure, an arterial bypass graft or angioplasty, kidney failure, liver failure, diabetes, hyperthyroidism or phaeochromocytoma.

Consult a pharmacist before using it together with paracetamol, caffeine, imipramine, oxazepam, pentazocine, propranolol, theophylline, warfarin, oestrogens, lignocaine, phenacetin, insulin, adrenergic antagonists (prazosin, labetalol and the like), flecainide, adrenergic agonists (isoprenaline, phenylephrine), propoxyphene, the diuretic furosemide, H2 antagonists, beta blockers, theophylline, tacrine, clozapine or ropinirole.

If any of the following occur, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: erythema (red patches), a burning sensation, blisters, skin rash or tightness at the site of application; agitation, anxiety, nervousness, insomnia, abnormal dreams, headache, dizziness, dyskinesia, disturbance of attention, somnolence (drowsiness), emotional instability, irritability, depression, confusion, tremor; palpitations, high blood pressure, flushing, chest pain, difficulty breathing, arrhythmia, cough, upper respiratory tract infection; nausea, abdominal pain, indigestion, vomiting, constipation, diarrhoea, abdominal distension, dry mouth; skin reactions at the site of application, excessive sweating, skin discoloration, cutaneous vasculitis, pain and discomfort at the site of application; muscle pain, arthritis, weakness, joint pain, muscle spasm, back pain; urticaria, rash, itching, angioedema or an anaphylactoid reaction.

summaryTable.What it is for: Aid when stopping smoking

groups.title: Capsule (A97900ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as adjunctive treatment for damaged hair, for poor growth of the nails that is not caused by infection, and for hair loss.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Children aged 12 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 1 to 2 times in 1 day, after meals. The average duration of treatment is 3 to 6 months.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child under 12 years of age, or for hair loss caused by scarring, androgenetic hereditary alopecia or male-pattern baldness.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Consult a pharmacist before using it together with a sulfonamide preparation.

If gastrointestinal discomfort (stomach pain, vomiting), sweating, tachycardia, itching, urticaria, headache, dizziness, flushing, or growth of hair on parts of the body other than the head occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Adjunctive treatment of damaged hair, poor nail growth not caused by infection, and hair loss

groups.title: Capsule (146602ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the improvement of symptoms related to venous insufficiency (a feeling of heaviness in the legs, pain and the like), as adjunctive treatment of disorders caused by capillary fragility, and for the treatment of signs related to haemorrhoids.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day (with lunch and with dinner). If haemorrhoids recur or become worse, up to 4 to 6 capsules (1200 to 1800 mg) may be taken in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or if you are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant.

Do not take it over a long period. If symptoms do not improve quickly, examination of the anus and a review of the treatment are needed.

If digestive disturbance occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Symptoms of venous insufficiency, disorders caused by capillary fragility, and signs related to haemorrhoids

groups.title: Capsule (187502ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for its antacid action and for the improvement of symptoms in gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis and excess stomach acid, and for constipation.
groups.usage: For gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis and excess stomach acid: take 1 to 2 capsules (0.5 to 1 g as magnesium oxide) in 1 day, divided into several doses. For constipation: take 4 capsules (2 g) in 1 day, divided into 1 to 2 doses. For the first dose, take the smallest amount and then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have kidney impairment or diarrhoea.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have impaired heart function, hypermagnesaemia, or if you are an older person (aged 65 years or older).

Because the adsorbent action of this medicine or the rise in the pH of the fluid in the digestive tract may affect the absorption and excretion of medicines taken with it, it should be given with care.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take tetracycline antibiotics. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with a large amount of milk or with calcium preparations.

If dizziness on standing up, slowing of the pulse, strong drowsiness, clouding of consciousness, a feeling of suffocation, muscle weakness, dry mouth or vomiting occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Symptoms of magnesium poisoning and, occasionally, diarrhoea may occur.

summaryTable.What it is for: Antacid action and symptom relief in gastric and duodenal ulcer, gastritis and excess stomach acid, and constipation

groups.title: Enteric-Coated Capsule (303404ACE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 1 capsule (100 mg) per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
An overdose in a child aged 6 years or younger can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is an infant under 12 months of age; or if you have haemochromatosis, haemosiderosis, impaired iron utilisation (anaemia due to lead poisoning, sideroachrestic anaemia, thalassaemia, porphyria cutanea tarda), anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency (megaloblastic anaemia due to vitamin B12 deficiency), anaemia due to bone marrow failure, chronic haemolytic anaemia, iron overload, iron deficiency anaemia caused by infection or a tumour, chronic pancreatitis, liver cirrhosis, or a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis, impaired heart or circulatory function, paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria, kidney impairment, hypoproteinaemia, if you are being given an iron-containing preparation (an iron supplement, an MRI liver contrast agent and the like), if you have delayed gastric emptying, pyloric stenosis or a gastrointestinal diverticulum, or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline antibiotics or antacids. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an anti-aldosterone medicine, triamterene, iron preparations and diphosphonate salts, thyroxine, a cefdinir preparation, salicylic acid, phenylbutazone, oxyphenbutazone with iron preparations, a quinolone, penicillamine, cholestyramine, pancreatic extract or a preparation such as vitamin E. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea, and milk and dairy products, while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: urticaria, itching, skin hypersensitivity on exposure to sunlight, abdominal or stomach pain, stomach cramps, vomiting, diarrhoea, fever, coma, nausea, loss of appetite, constipation, black stools, tooth discoloration, stomach discomfort; occasionally raised AST and ALT; rarely raised ALP.

summaryTable.What it is for: Prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia

groups.title: Soft Capsule (A50200ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamin E and vitamin B2 in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness, and in old age, and for the relief of peripheral circulatory disturbance, stiffness of the shoulder and neck at the menopause, numbness and coldness of the hands and feet, angular cheilitis (inflammation at the corners of the mouth), cheilitis (inflammation of the lips), stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), glossitis (inflammation of the tongue), eczema and dermatitis.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 8 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to soybean oil, soybean or peanut, or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; if a particular risk is expected from fat overload; if you have a tendency to thrombosis; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. It may turn the urine yellow and may affect the results of clinical tests.

Consult a pharmacist before using it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen or with an intravenous lipid preparation.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, nausea, loss of appetite or a feeling of fullness in the abdomen occurs, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected, the amount gradually increases, or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamin E and B2 and relief of peripheral circulatory disturbance, shoulder and neck stiffness at the menopause, numb and cold hands and feet, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis

groups.title: Eye Drops (D01200COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for eye fatigue, for supplementing tears (dryness of the eye), for discomfort while wearing hard or soft contact lenses, and for blurred eyes (when there is a lot of eye discharge).
groups.usage: Instil 1 to 3 drops per dose, 3 to 6 times in 1 day. After instillation, discard the remaining solution and the container immediately.
groups.caution:
Consult a pharmacist if you have severe eye pain, if you have ever had an allergic reaction to an eye medicine (redness of the eye, itching, swelling, rash, reddening and the like), or if you have glaucoma.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If blurring of the eyes does not improve with this medicine, stop using it and consult a pharmacist. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only. To prevent contamination, do not share it with others. After opening, use it only once immediately and discard the remaining solution and the container at once. Do not let the tip of the container touch the eyelid or the eyelashes, and do not use the solution if it is cloudy.

If redness of the eye, itching or swelling occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Eye fatigue, tear supplementation (dry eye), discomfort with contact lenses and blurred eyes

groups.title: Medicated Gum (A87801AMS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as an aid to stopping smoking; it reduces the amount smoked and helps you to give up cigarettes.
groups.usage: For adults, the 2 mg gum is recommended for smokers of 20 or fewer cigarettes a day, and the 4 mg gum is recommended for heavy smokers of more than 20 cigarettes a day or when the 2 mg strength has not worked. Use it whenever there is an urge to smoke.
groups.caution:
It may stick to dental prostheses and dentures and, in rare cases, may damage them.

Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, unstable angina, worsening angina, myocardial infarction within the past 3 months, the late phase after an acute infarction, severe cardiac arrhythmia, systemic hypertension, peripheral vascular disease, acute stroke or cerebrovascular disease; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child or adolescent under 18 years of age; or if the user is a non-smoker or an occasional smoker.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have gastritis, gastric or duodenal ulcer, occlusive arterial disease, stable angina, heart failure, decompensated heart failure, myocardial infarction, cardiac arrhythmia, vasospasm, uncontrolled high blood pressure, an arterial bypass graft or angioplasty; if you are an older person; if you have kidney failure, liver failure, diabetes, hyperthyroidism or phaeochromocytoma; if you are a smoker with dentures; or if you have had epilepsy or seizures.

Chewing it quickly may sometimes cause unpleasant symptoms, so chew it slowly. Chewing several pieces at the same time may cause serious symptoms of overdose, so do not chew several pieces at once.

Consult a pharmacist before using it together with paracetamol, caffeine, imipramine, oxazepam, pentazocine, propranolol, theophylline, warfarin, oestrogens, lignocaine, phenacetin, insulin, adrenergic antagonists (prazosin, labetalol and the like), flecainide, adrenergic agonists (isoprenaline, phenylephrine), propoxyphene, the diuretic furosemide, H2 antagonists, beta blockers, tacrine, clozapine, ropinirole, olanzapine, clomipramine or fluvoxamine.

If any of the following occur, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: headache, dizziness, sleep disturbance, anxiety, emotional instability, agitation, abnormal dreams, confusion, restlessness, difficulty concentrating, fatigue, migraine, spasm, leg cramps, seizures; changes in blood pressure, high blood pressure, palpitations, reversible atrial fibrillation, atrial arrhythmia; nausea, vomiting, upper abdominal pain, abdominal pain, indigestion, flatulence (abdominal distension), gastrointestinal disorders such as gastric ulcer, difficulty swallowing, thirst, abnormal bowel movements, constipation, diarrhoea, increased appetite; cold and influenza symptoms, cough, pharyngitis, rhinitis, sinusitis, upper respiratory symptoms, bronchitis, difficulty breathing; allergy, skin eruption, herpes eruption, itching, urticaria, acne, erythema (red patches); distortion of taste, abnormal vision, irritation (pain) of the mouth and throat, pain of the jaw joint and muscles, gingivitis; dysmenorrhoea, muscle pain, joint pain, toothache, back pain, chest pain, pain, earache, facial flushing, local swelling, weight gain, thyroid dysfunction, pain of the lymph nodes, cystitis, increased sweating, hiccups or angioedema.

summaryTable.What it is for: Aid to stopping smoking; reduces the amount smoked

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for eye fatigue, for supplementing tears (dryness of the eye), for discomfort while wearing hard or soft contact lenses, and for blurred eyes (when there is a lot of eye discharge).
groups.usage: Instil 1 to 3 drops per dose, 3 to 6 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to eye medicines, severe eye pain or glaucoma.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only. To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with others.

If redness of the eye, itching or swelling occurs, or if a wearer of hard contact lenses has a lot of discharge such as eye mucus or the lenses become cloudy, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (241101ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for vitamin E deficiency, for impaired peripheral circulation, and for the relief of symptoms such as stiffness of the shoulder and neck at the menopause, numbness and coldness of the hands and feet, intermittent claudication (occasional limping) and frostbite.
groups.usage: Adults: take 50 IU to 1000 IU of vitamin E in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you have hypersensitivity to soybean oil, soybean or peanut, or if you are breast-feeding. Avoid taking high doses of this medicine during pregnancy.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant; if you have a tendency to thrombosis; if you have had bronchial asthma, rash or urticaria; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if a particular risk is expected from fat overload; if the user is a child taking an iron preparation; or if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 or Yellow No. 5.

Consult a pharmacist before using it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, vitamin A or vitamin K preparations, oral anticoagulants, the anti-obesity medicine orlistat, a mineral-oil laxative, an iron preparation or an intravenous lipid preparation.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, nausea, muscle weakness, fatigue, headache or blurred vision (with long-term use) occurs, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected, the amount gradually increases, or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Granules (A69800AGN)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for haemorrhoids (internal piles), anal fissure and bleeding from haemorrhoids.
groups.usage: Adults aged 15 years and older: take 1 sachet per dose, 2 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
This medicine contains aspartame, which is metabolised in the body to phenylalanine, so it must not be taken by people with phenylketonuria who need to restrict their intake of phenylalanine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child under 15 years of age, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant, or if you have had allergic symptoms.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

If rash, reddening of the skin or itching, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting or, rarely, diarrhoea occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Haemorrhoids, anal fissure and bleeding from haemorrhoids

groups.title: Tablet (265300ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of blocked nose, runny nose, sneezing, watering eyes, sore throat and a heavy head caused by a head cold (acute rhinitis), allergic rhinitis or sinusitis.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking this medicine and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if the user is an infant under 3 months of age; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; or if you have severe acute or chronic kidney disease or renal failure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic reactions (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have heart disease, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you are an older person; if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache; if you have symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like); or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like). Do not take it together with other oral medicines for rhinitis or with oral medicines containing antihistamines (cold medicines, antitussive-expectorants, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines and the like). Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: haemorrhagic stroke, nausea or vomiting, persistent or severe thirst, constipation, loss of appetite, rash or reddening of the skin, itching, difficulty passing urine, or rarely symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome and reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance).

summaryTable.What it is for: Blocked nose, runny nose, sneezing, watering eyes, sore throat and heavy head from a head cold, allergic rhinitis or sinusitis

groups.title: Enteric-Coated Tablet (A55800ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 to 3 tablets per dose, 1 time in 1 day, at bedtime (on an empty stomach). For the first dose, take the smallest amount and then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like), intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), or a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is a child aged 10 years or younger; if you have an allergic constitution; if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you have kidney impairment; if you are on a sodium-restricted diet; if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist. Do not chew the tablets when taking them.

Do not take it together with an antacid. Avoid taking it within 1 hour after drinking milk.

If rash or reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Constipation and the loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal intestinal fermentation and haemorrhoids that accompany it

groups.title: Eye Gel (109130COO)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as a lubricating aid to protect and lubricate the eye: in keratitis sicca (dry keratitis, for use at night), during eye surgery, to protect and lubricate the eye that is not being operated on, as a lubricant after surgery, and to protect and lubricate the eye during surgery other than eye surgery.
groups.usage: Apply a small amount (0.5 cm) into the conjunctival sac.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have eye discharge, watering of the eye or redness; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child; or if you have liver impairment or kidney impairment.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Contact lens wearers must remove their lenses before using this medicine and may put them back in 30 minutes after using it. If another eye preparation is used at the same time, allow an interval of at least 5 minutes and always use this medicine last. Temporary blurring of vision or other visual disturbance may occur, so take care when driving or operating machinery. To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with others. Do not use it after the expiry date, and use it within 30 days of opening.

Do not use a preservative or a cleaning solution while you are using this medicine.

If eye pain, discomfort, irritation, swelling, redness of the eye, increased tear production, headache, a change in vision or persistent redness occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Protecting and lubricating the eye in keratitis sicca and during and after surgery

groups.title: Enteric-Coated Tablet (451201ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of inflammatory symptoms accompanied by swelling and for swelling after injury or surgery.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet (100 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day, 30 minutes before meals, with water. Much about how it works in the body is still unexplained and the relationship between dose and effect has not been established, so do not take it without a clear purpose.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have a severe blood clotting disorder (haemophilia and the like), severe liver disease or severe kidney disease (including patients on haemodialysis), if you are being given an anticoagulant or an antiplatelet medicine, if you are pregnant or breast-feeding, or if the user is a child under 12 years of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Do not take it together with an anticoagulant or an antiplatelet medicine. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an antibiotic (tetracycline and the like).

If, rarely, a hypersensitivity reaction, stomach pain or diarrhoea occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Inflammatory symptoms with swelling, and swelling after injury or surgery

groups.title: Oral Solution (C10900ALQ)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for nutritional supply during the recovery period of an illness or after it and in wasting diseases, and for physical fatigue and as a tonic.
groups.usage: Take 1 bottle (vial) per dose, 1 time in 1 day, between meals.

For a young child who has difficulty swallowing the tablet, place the tablet on a spoon, let it disintegrate in water and, if possible, give it with a meal. When it is put into food, add it after the food has been boiled; if the food is rich in vitamin D, the dose may need to be adjusted.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is an infant under 3 months of age, or if you have hypercalcaemia, hypercalciuria, kidney stones, or a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is an infant under 1 year of age; if the child gets a lot of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you have had kidney stones; if you have sarcoidosis; if your movement is restricted (for example in a plaster cast); if you have pseudohypoparathyroidism or kidney impairment; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

If more than 500 IU a day is given, monitor blood and urine calcium levels and kidney function regularly.

Do not take it together with a benzothiadiazine derivative. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with another vitamin D preparation, phenytoin, barbiturates, thiazide diuretics or glucocorticoids.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: mental symptoms, disturbance of consciousness (raised serum calcium), headache, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, weight loss, increased thirst (raised serum calcium), arrhythmia, increased urge to pass urine, kidney stones, nephrocalcinosis, calcification in the tissue around the bones, muscle pain or joint pain.

groups.title: Capsule (B96700ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, sputum, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine; if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain, an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines). Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid or flucloxacillin. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, high anion gap metabolic acidosis; rarely signs of shock (urticaria and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters); asthma; general lassitude; jaundice; or interstitial pneumonia (cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever).

groups.title: Eye Drops (B36200COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for eye fatigue, conjunctival congestion, prevention of eye disease (after swimming, when dust or sweat gets into the eye and the like), inflammation of the eye caused by ultraviolet or other light (such as snow ophthalmia), blepharitis (inflammation and soreness of the eyelid), discomfort while wearing hard contact lenses, itching of the eye, and blurred eyes (when there is a lot of eye discharge).
groups.usage: Instil 2 to 3 drops per dose, 5 to 6 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine in young children aged 30 months or younger, and do not use it when wearing soft lenses or while soft contact lenses are in the eye.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe eye pain, if you have had allergic symptoms (redness of the eye, itching, swelling, rash, reddening and the like), if you have glaucoma, or if the user is a child.

When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Use this medicine for instillation into the eye only. To prevent contamination, avoid sharing it with others.

If redness of the eye, itching or swelling, skin rash, reddening of the skin or itching occurs, or if blurring of the eyes does not improve, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. To make up for the loss of fluid caused by diarrhoea, drink plenty of fluids containing salt or sugar.

If you continue to eat during diarrhoea, do not eat raw food, fruit, vegetables, spicy food, or frozen food or drinks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have peptic ulcer; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you have pus or purulent sputum, fever, or chronic bronchial or lung disease.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after several doses, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist. If digestive disturbance occurs (abdominal pain, vomiting, diarrhoea), reduce the dose.

Do not take it together with a preparation that suppresses cough and sputum (atropine-type medicines).

Allergic skin reactions such as itching, urticaria, erythematous rash and swelling of the face and, very rarely, anaphylaxis may occur.

groups.title: Capsule (D93900ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: take 1 1/3 capsules per dose. Ages 8 years to under 11 years: take 1 capsule per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage. Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately. Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma with another antipyretic analgesic or cold medicine; if the user is an infant under 3 months of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is an infant or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child under 2 years of age; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you are an older person or physically weak; if you have an allergic constitution; if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you have a high fever, heartburn, stomach discomfort, stomach pain, an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinson medicines and the like), antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines), or preparations containing diphenhydramine. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants, alcohol, a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant or a steroid. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness; signs of shock (urticaria and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters); asthma; general lassitude; jaundice; or interstitial pneumonia (cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever).
