groups.title: Tablet (142302ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthrosis, ankylosing spondylitis, painful swelling or inflammation after injury and surgery, and as an aid in the treatment of infections accompanied by inflammation, pain and fever.
groups.usage: Children aged 6 years and older: take about 15 mg per kg of body weight in 1 day, divided into 2 to 4 doses. In children weighing less than 30 kg the daily dose must not exceed 2 tablets (300 mg). Adults: take 2 tablets (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 4 times in 1 day, with meals; do not exceed 8 tablets (1200 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious cardiovascular adverse reactions may occur.

Taking this medicine may cause serious and possibly fatal gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as bleeding, ulceration and perforation of the gastrointestinal tract.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer; if you have bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels or elsewhere; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe heart failure or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; for the treatment of pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery; if you are 6 months or more pregnant; if you have inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis; if you have had gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation during treatment with a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have fluid retention or heart failure, high blood pressure, or a history of hypersensitivity; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD); if you are an older person; if the user is a child aged 6 years or older; if you have stomach cancer or alcoholism; if you are in early or mid pregnancy or may be pregnant; if you have ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease or risk factors for cardiovascular disease (for example high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking); if you have hepatic porphyria; if you have had major surgery with blood loss; if you are being given a diuretic or an ACE inhibitor; or if you have a blood clotting disorder or are being given an anticoagulant.

Considering the importance of the treatment, either stop breast-feeding or stop taking the medicine. Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. When it is taken for a long period for an acute illness, as a rule this should be within 5 days.

Do not take it together with aspirin, another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, or high-dose methotrexate. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking a corticosteroid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin II receptor antagonist, a diuretic, lithium, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), baclofen, an immunosuppressant (ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus), a thrombolytic, ticlopidine, an antithrombotic, a medicine that raises blood potassium (for example a potassium-sparing diuretic, an ACE inhibitor, an angiotensin II receptor antagonist, an immunosuppressant such as ciclosporin or tacrolimus, trimethoprim or heparin), an inducer of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (for example rifampicin or phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg a week), an antiplatelet medicine, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, or low-dose aspirin.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); rarely blood disorders such as aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; indigestion, abdominal distension, heartburn, upper abdominal pain, diarrhoea or constipation; occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain or stomach discomfort; rarely oesophagitis, oesophageal stricture, worsening of diverticula, non-specific haemorrhagic colitis, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, bloody stools, gastritis or pancreatitis; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, erythema multiforme, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or hair loss; occasionally angioedema; rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; occasionally rash, urticaria, itching or purpura; rarely triggering of an asthma attack, eczema, an anaphylactic reaction or a photosensitivity reaction; rarely jaundice, raised ALT, raised AST, raised ALP, abnormal liver function, hepatitis or jaundice; occasionally rhinitis, bronchospasm or acute pneumonia; rarely visual disturbance such as scotoma or dark spots, hearing loss, tinnitus or taste disturbance; fatigue, drowsiness, headache or dizziness; occasionally anxiety, restlessness, confusion or depression; rarely aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness; rarely mental disturbance, agitation, excitement, disorientation or reversible toxic amblyopia; rarely a fall in blood pressure, a rise in blood pressure, palpitations, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine (reduced kidney function), high blood potassium, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; rarely renal papillary necrosis, nephrotic syndrome, interstitial nephritis, peripheral oedema, acute pulmonary oedema, fluid retention, high blood pressure or heart failure; Conn's syndrome or reduced fertility in women, of unknown frequency; occasionally swelling around the eye sockets; very rarely malaise, fever, nosebleed or worsening of inflammation.

groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Serious skin reactions such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking this medicine, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergic reaction to a medicine (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; or if you have a cough (smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache).

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like), antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines). Consult a pharmacist if you have been given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema (swelling), difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness; rarely signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters over the whole skin or on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes); asthma; liver function disorder (general lassitude, jaundice with yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes and the like); or interstitial pneumonia (cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever).

groups.title: Tablet (145901ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for nausea, vomiting and dizziness caused by motion sickness, Meniere's syndrome or radiation sickness, and for nausea and vomiting after surgery.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet (50 mg) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. For prevention, take 1 to 2 tablets (50 to 100 mg) 30 minutes to 1 hour beforehand. As a rule do not exceed 4 tablets (200 mg) in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to meclizine hydrochloride or buclizine hydrochloride; if you have difficulty passing urine such as that caused by prostatic hyperplasia; if you have narrow-angle glaucoma or epilepsy; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child; if you have hyperthyroidism or acute nephritis; if you are about to be given an anaesthetic; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you are an older person.

Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor. Consult a pharmacist before using it together with barbiturates or another central nervous system depressant such as an anaesthetic, an aminoglycoside antibiotic (streptomycin, kanamycin and the like), or atropine and atropine-type medicines. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash or photosensitivity occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Drowsiness, headache, a heavy head, numbness of the hands and feet, tremor of the fingers, dizziness, visual disturbance such as blurred vision, insomnia, abnormal sensation and, occasionally, heartburn, stomach pain, difficulty passing urine, dry mouth and tiredness may occur.

groups.title: Tablet (D39300ATB)

Do not take more than 8 tablets in 1 day. People aged 60 years and older: dissolve 2 tablets completely in water (about 120 mL) and take them when needed, at intervals of 4 hours. Do not take more than 4 tablets in 1 day.
groups.caution:
A person under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza must consult a doctor before taking this medicine.

Aspirin can cause serious allergic reactions (urticaria, swelling of the face, asthma, shock).

If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

This medicine contains a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (NSAID), which can cause serious gastrointestinal bleeding. The risk of gastrointestinal bleeding may be increased in people aged 60 years and older, in people with gastric ulcer or a bleeding disorder, in people taking an anticoagulant or a steroid, in people taking another medicine containing a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, and when more than the stated dose is taken or it is taken for longer than stated.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had a hypersensitivity reaction to aspirin or another salicylate preparation or to another antipyretic analgesic; if you have or have had aspirin asthma (an asthma attack triggered by a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic and the like); if you need to restrict your sodium intake; if you have peptic ulcer, haemophilia or a tendency to bleed; if you have severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment or severe cardiac insufficiency; or if you are in the third trimester of pregnancy.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; if you are an older person; if you have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have had gastrointestinal disturbance; if you have high blood pressure, heart disease, liver disease or kidney disease; if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are about to have surgery; or if you have severe glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency or an electrolyte disturbance such as hypochloraemic alkalosis.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not take it continuously for a long period.

While taking this medicine, do not take it together with high-dose methotrexate (15 mg a week or more), another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or a salicylate preparation. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with a diuretic, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, a steroid, an anticoagulant, a thrombolytic, another antiplatelet medicine, a haemostatic, a diabetes medicine (insulin preparations, tolbutamide and the like), a uricosuric (benzbromarone, probenecid), low-dose methotrexate, a lithium preparation, ibuprofen, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, digoxin, a systemically acting adrenocortical hormone preparation (except hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), an ACE inhibitor or valproic acid. groups.title: Tablet (E30001ATB)

groups.usage: Take the tablets every day at about the same time with water, in the order shown on the pack. groups.caution:

groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have had an allergic reaction or allergic symptoms (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you have stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, an ulcer or a bleeding problem; if you have lost a lot of fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea or cannot take in fluid; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5; or if the user is a child under 2 years of age.

Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines). Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with a diuretic, a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, stomach pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, stomach discomfort, hearing loss, oedema, tinnitus, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness; rarely signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing); Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome: severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters over the whole skin or on the mucous membranes of the mouth or eyes); asthma; general lassitude; jaundice; or interstitial pneumonia (cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever).

Do not use it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like), another antitussive-expectorant, a cold medicine, an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine), a sedative, or a preparation containing diphenhydramine (including preparations applied to the skin). Do not take this medicine if you have stopped taking an MAO inhibitor within the past 2 weeks. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, dizziness, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, palpitations, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (D66800ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, cough, sputum, sore throat, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Those aged 15 years and older: take 1 sachet (20 mL) per dose. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: 2/3 sachet per dose. Ages 7 years to under 11 years: 1/2 sachet per dose. Ages 3 years to under 7 years: 1/3 sachet per dose. Ages 2 years to under 3 years: 1/4 sachet per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have ever had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have a constitution prone to urticaria, contact dermatitis, bronchial asthma, allergic rhinitis, migraine or food allergy; if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you are an older person; if you have gastric or duodenal ulcer; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you have a cough (smoking, asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache).

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not take it continuously for a long period. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, MAO inhibitors (antidepressants, antipsychotics, mood stabilisers, antiparkinson medicines and the like), antitussive-expectorants, other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines). Do not take this medicine if you have stopped taking an MAO inhibitor within the past 2 weeks. Consult a pharmacist if you have been given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia; rarely urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms such as high fever with rash, reddening and burn-like blisters); acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; severe skin reactions with fever, erythema and many small pustules; asthma; general lassitude; jaundice; interstitial pneumonia (cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing and fever); or symptoms of ischaemic colitis in connection with pseudoephedrine (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding).

If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome occur (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance and the like), stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Cream (143331CCM)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of pain and inflammation in traumatic inflammation of tendons, ligaments, muscles and joints (sprains, bruises and the like), in localised forms of soft tissue rheumatic disease (tenosynovitis, shoulder-hand syndrome, bursitis, periarthritis and the like) and in localised forms of rheumatic disease (osteoarthritis of the peripheral joints and the spine and the like).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: apply 2 to 4 g per dose to the affected area, 3 to 4 times in 1 day according to the size of the painful area, and rub it in gently. Without the instruction of a doctor, this medicine must not be used for more than 7 days for muscle and joint injury, and it must not be used for more than 14 days.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had hypersensitivity such as asthma, angioedema, urticaria or acute rhinitis caused by aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if the user is a child under 12 years of age; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are an older person, if you have bronchial asthma, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to propylene glycol.

This medicine is for external use on the skin only; do not take it by mouth. Do not use it on damaged skin (bleeding skin disease, eczema, infected lesions, burns, wounds) or on the eyes or mucous membranes. If symptoms do not improve or become worse after 7 days of use, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Do not breast-feed while using this medicine. Wash your hands thoroughly after use (except when it is used on the finger joints). Do not use it under an occlusive dressing. People using this medicine should refrain from smoking and take care not to go near a naked flame.

Consult a pharmacist if you are being given a loop diuretic (furosemide and the like), a thiazide diuretic, a medicine that interferes with clotting (warfarin and the like), an antiplatelet medicine (aspirin and the like), a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor or a serotonin-noradrenaline reuptake inhibitor.

If any of the following occur, stop using this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: commonly rash, eczema, erythema (red patches) and dermatitis (including contact dermatitis) or itching; rarely bullous dermatitis; very rarely hypersensitivity reactions (including urticaria), angioneurotic oedema, asthma, photosensitivity reactions or pustular rash.

If serious skin adverse reactions such as exfoliative dermatitis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis occur, or serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions including bleeding, ulceration or perforation of the stomach or intestine, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If the skin is damaged, use may cause temporary irritation and a tingling sensation, so take care.

groups.title: Tablet (135201ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for allergic rhinitis, hay fever, urticaria, itchy skin conditions (pruritus, eczema, dermatitis), angioneurotic oedema, and the sneezing, runny nose and cough caused by a head cold.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet (1 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day, in the morning and in the evening. Do not exceed 2 tablets (2 mg) in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a baby aged 1 year or younger; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to this medicine or to another antihistamine; if you have a lower respiratory tract disease such as an asthma attack; if you are being given an MAO inhibitor; if you have an obstructive disease of the lower urinary tract such as prostatic hyperplasia; if you have glaucoma; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Consult a pharmacist if you have stenosing peptic ulcer or pyloroduodenal obstruction, high blood pressure, a history of bronchial asthma, hyperthyroidism, cardiovascular disease, polyuria, a convulsive disorder such as epilepsy now or in the past, or hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4, or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with alcohol, a central nervous system depressant (hypnotic, sedative, tranquilliser and the like) or an anticholinergic medicine.

If urticaria, rash, drug eruption, anaphylactic shock, photosensitivity, sweating or chills occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Temporary drowsiness, low blood pressure, headache, palpitations, rapid heartbeat, extrasystoles, sedation, drowsiness, dizziness, incoordination, fatigue, confusion, anxiety, excitement, nervousness, tremor, irritability, insomnia, perversion of sensation, abnormal sensation, blurred vision, double vision, tinnitus, acute labyrinthitis, hysteria, a heavy head, lassitude and, occasionally, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, thirst, diarrhoea, indigestion, upper abdominal pain, digestive disturbance, constipation, haemolytic anaemia, thrombocytopenia, agranulocytosis, frequent urination, difficulty passing urine, urinary retention, early menstruation, thickening of bronchial secretions, wheezing or chest tightness, and blocked nose may occur.

groups.title: Tablet (D52700ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of headache, toothache, pain after tooth extraction, sore throat, earache, joint pain, neuralgia, back pain, muscle pain, stiff shoulder, pain from a bruise, pain from a fracture, pain from a sprain, menstrual pain and pain from injury, and for reducing fever with chills.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 to 3 times in 1 day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking this medicine, one of its ingredients, another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you are 30 weeks pregnant or more.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine such as fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching; or if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; or if you have lost a lot of fluid through vomiting and diarrhoea or cannot take in fluid.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Do not take it continuously for a long period. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

While you are taking this medicine, do not take another antipyretic analgesic, a cold medicine or a sedative. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are being given a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid or a diuretic. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash or reddening of the skin, itching, nausea or vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, gastrointestinal bleeding, stomach discomfort, dizziness or oedema occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If, rarely, shock (anaphylaxis) occurs with urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing, or if Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome) or asthma occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If, very rarely, erythema multiforme or exfoliative dermatitis occurs, or if drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs (frequency unknown), stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Relief of headache, toothache, sore throat, earache, joint, nerve, back and muscle pain, stiff shoulder, injury pain and menstrual pain, and reduction of fever

groups.title: Powder (411901APD)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 8 years and older: take 10 to 20 g (1 to 2 sachets) in 1 day. Depending on symptoms, and especially for children, 10 g (1 sachet) may be taken every second day. Dissolve 10 g (1 sachet) of this medicine in a cup of water and drink it. Taking it in the morning is recommended; the effect appears clearly within 1 to 2 days (24 to 48 hours) after taking it.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have inflammatory bowel disease (ulcerative colitis, Crohn's disease and the like); if you have toxic megacolon; if you have or are at risk of intestinal perforation; if you have or are suspected of having intestinal obstruction; if you have intestinal stricture; or if you have abdominal pain of unknown cause.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child under 8 years of age; if you have acute constipation that is not caused by a change in lifestyle; if you have acute constipation with pain, fever or abdominal distension; or if you have irritable bowel syndrome.

Consult a pharmacist if you use it together with a diuretic.

In adults, if abdominal pain and distension, diarrhoea, nausea, vomiting, urgent need to open the bowels, faecal incontinence, electrolyte disturbance (low blood sodium, low blood potassium) and dehydration, or a hypersensitivity reaction (itching, rash, facial swelling, angioedema, urticaria, anaphylactic shock) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. In children, if abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal distension, nausea or a hypersensitivity reaction occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Orally Dissolving Film (566801ATD)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of selenium in people with selenium deficiency that cannot be made up by nutritional intake.
groups.usage: Use 1 film per dose; the amount may be increased to a maximum of 2 films in 1 day. Do not chew it and do not swallow it; let it dissolve slowly in the mouth.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a baby under 12 months of age, or if you have selenium toxicity.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; or if the user is a child under 12 years of age.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not use it together with a reducing agent such as vitamin C. If you want to take vitamin C, take it separately with an interval of about 4 hours from this medicine. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while using it and just before and after using it.

If dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, vomiting or allergy occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E24800ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins D, E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in old age; for the prevention of poor development of bones and teeth and of rickets; for the relief of neuralgia, muscle pain, joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulder and the like), beriberi, eye fatigue, angular cheilitis (inflammation at the corners of the mouth), cheilitis (inflammation of the lips), stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), glossitis (inflammation of the tongue), eczema and dermatitis; and for the supply of zinc.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day, after a meal.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have hypercalcaemia (an excess of calcium in the blood), sarcoidosis (a systemic inflammatory disease of unknown cause), kidney disease, kidney stones or severe renal failure; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if the child gets a lot of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have hyperoxaluria (a state in which an excessive amount of oxalate is excreted in the urine); if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment, hypoproteinaemia or gout; if you have had kidney stones; if you have a tendency to thrombosis; or if you are short of folic acid.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. It may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, affecting the results of clinical tests. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with cardiac glycosides, an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, loose stools, stomatitis, low blood pressure, facial flushing, irregular heartbeat, skin rash, red patches, asystole (stopping of the heartbeat), reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, pulmonary oedema, or menstruation that comes earlier than expected, gradually increases in amount or lasts a long time.

groups.title: Tablet (172601ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of anxiety, listlessness and mild, temporary depressive symptoms.
groups.usage: Adults and children aged 12 years and older: take 1 tablet (300 mg of St John's wort 80% methanol dry extract) per dose, 3 times in 1 day, with a small amount of water, without chewing it.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have severe depression; if you have had a skin photosensitivity reaction; if you are pregnant, may become pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a child under 12 years of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

While you are taking this medicine, avoid strong exposure to ultraviolet light (long sunbathing, sun lamps, tanning beds). Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not use it together with antiretroviral medicines or medicines for chronic hepatitis C (efavirenz, nevirapine, delavirdine, lamivudine, zidovudine, stavudine, abacavir, didanosine, zalcitabine, indinavir, saquinavir, ritonavir, nelfinavir, amprenavir, sofosbuvir, ledipasvir and the like), anticoagulants (acenocoumarol, phenprocoumon, warfarin, dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban and the like), cytostatic medicines (irinotecan, cyclophosphamide, tamoxifen, taxol, etoposide and the like) or immunosuppressants (ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus, everolimus and the like).

Consult a pharmacist if you use it together with cardiac medicines (digitoxin, digoxin, metildigoxin and the like), bronchodilators (aminophylline, choline theophyllinate, theophylline and the like), antiarrhythmics (amiodarone, quinidine, disopyramide, propafenone, lidocaine and the like), anticonvulsants (phenobarbital, phenytoin, carbamazepine, primidone and the like), sedative-hypnotics (midazolam and the like), oral or injectable contraceptives (ethinylestradiol, desogestrel, norethisterone, levonorgestrel and the like) or contraceptive devices containing these medicines (including implants), migraine medicines (sumatriptan, naratriptan, rizatriptan, zolmitriptan and the like), antidepressants such as selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (imipramine, amitriptyline, nortriptyline, citalopram, fluoxetine, fluvoxamine, paroxetine, sertraline, nefazodone, escitalopram, venlafaxine and the like), methadone, lipid-lowering medicines (certain HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors such as simvastatin, but not pravastatin), steroid hormones (oral or intravenous), non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics, arthritis treatments (COX-2 inhibitors), antihypertensives (calcium channel blockers), oral blood-glucose-lowering medicines (metformin) or other blood-glucose-regulating medicines, or narcotic analgesics.

If an allergic skin reaction (reddening, itching), a photosensitivity reaction with increased sensitivity of the skin to sunlight, fatigue, anxiety, drowsiness, agitation or gastrointestinal disturbance occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (E76600ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamins A, B1, B2, B6, C, D and E in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in old age; for the relief of dryness of the eyes; for night blindness (difficulty seeing at night); for the prevention of poor development of bones and teeth and of rickets; and for the prevention and treatment of iron deficiency anaemia.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 8 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Taking 5,000 IU or more of vitamin A a day may cause birth defects. Women who are within the first 3 months of pregnancy or who may be pregnant must not take it.

An overdose in a child aged 6 years or younger can cause fatal iron poisoning, so keep this medicine out of the reach of children.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, hypercalcaemia, sarcoidosis, kidney disease or kidney stones; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have haemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas because of abnormal iron metabolism) or haemosiderosis; if you have anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency; if you have kidney stones or severe renal failure (reduced kidney function); or if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to Yellow No. 5.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are under treatment by a doctor; if the child gets a lot of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you have hyperoxaluria; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you have peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have gout; or if you have or have had kidney stones.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is used for a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. It may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, affecting the results of clinical tests.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. In women taking an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, or in people with a tendency to thrombosis, taking vitamin E may increase the risk of thrombosis (blockage of a blood vessel), so take care. Do not take it together with an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene; this may cause high blood potassium. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: itching, dry and rough skin, cramps, photosensitivity reactions, nausea, vomiting, urticaria, loose stools, reddening of the skin, rash, constipation, abdominal or stomach pain, asystole (stopping of the heartbeat), red patches, upper abdominal pain, diarrhoea, digestive disturbance, fever, stomach discomfort, gastrointestinal disturbance, low blood pressure, reduced central nervous system function, painful swelling of the joints, pulmonary oedema, coma, or menstruation that comes earlier than expected, gradually increases in amount or lasts a long time.

groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the supply of vitamin D and vitamin B2 in physical fatigue, during pregnancy and breast-feeding, when physical strength is reduced during or after an illness, during growth and in old age, and for the prevention of poor development of bones and teeth and of rickets.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 8 years and older: take 1 capsule per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:

To prevent the medicine from spreading to other parts of the body or infecting other people, apply it while wearing a finger cot or rubber gloves.

Discomfort such as tenderness, a temporary burning sensation, mild pain including stinging, contact dermatitis, erythematous rash, eczema and allergic reactions and, occasionally, irritation at the site of application, itching, vulvitis, facial swelling, skin discoloration, urticaria, rash, vesicular rash and peeling of the skin may occur.

groups.usage: Those aged 19 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if the user is a baby under 12 months of age; if you have hypercalcaemia, sarcoidosis, kidney disease, kidney stones or severe renal failure; if you have had hypersensitivity or an allergic reaction to soybean oil; or if you have hypersensitivity to soybean or peanut.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or a young child; if you are an older person; if you have hyperoxaluria; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have gout or kidney stones now or in the past; or if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. It may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests and may turn the urine yellow, affecting the results of clinical tests.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen. Taking it together with an anti-aldosterone medicine or triamterene may cause high blood potassium, so take care. Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea while taking it and just before and after taking it.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, constipation, rash, reddening of the skin, loose stools, stomatitis (inflammation inside the mouth), red patches, asystole (stopping of the heartbeat), reduced central nervous system function, dermatitis, a bad smell in the sweat or breath, hair loss, irritability, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, low blood pressure or pulmonary oedema occurs, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected, gradually increases in amount or lasts a long time, or if symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Apply an appropriate amount to the affected area, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not use this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding, or if the user is a baby or a child.

Do not use it on the eyes or around the eyes, on mucous membranes (inside the mouth, inside the nose, the vagina), on the scrotum or the external genitals, on eczema, on areas that are wet, eroded, cracked or severely wounded, on the nails or on the scalp.

Before using this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution, if the affected area is on the face or is extensive or has become purulent, or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to propylene glycol.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not use it while the affected area or the skin around it is dirty. Do not touch the eyes or mucous membranes with hands that have this medicine on them. Take care not to let it get into the eyes; if it does, wash it out immediately with cold or lukewarm water. Use this medicine externally only.

If rash, reddening of the skin, itching, swelling, irritation, a hot feeling, scaling, flaking of the skin, erosion, dry or tight skin, or cracking of the skin occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have haemochromatosis (a disease in which iron is deposited in the liver and pancreas because of abnormal iron metabolism), haemosiderosis, anaemia that is not due to iron deficiency or pernicious anaemia; if you have hypersensitivity to soybean oil, soybean or peanut; or if the user is a baby under 12 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional enteritis; if you have hyperoxaluria (a state in which an excessive amount of oxalate is excreted in the urine); if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney impairment or hypoproteinaemia; if you have a disorder of fat metabolism such as hyperlipoproteinaemia, diabetic hyperlipidaemia or pancreatitis, or if lipid emulsions must be given to you with caution; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. It may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests.

Do not take it together with phosphate salts, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids containing calcium carbonate or magnesium hydroxide, or allopurinol. Consult a pharmacist before taking it together with an anti-aldosterone medicine, triamterene or 200 mg or more of ascorbic acid (vitamin C). Avoid tannin-containing drinks such as green tea and black tea, and milk and dairy products, while taking it and just before and after taking it.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (E58100ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, sputum, chills, fever, headache, joint pain and muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Ages over 7 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule per dose, 3 times in 1 day. Take it 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have ever had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had an allergy caused by a medicine (fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching and the like); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision and the like) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. Do not drink alcohol while taking it. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. Do not take it continuously for a long period.

Do not take it together with an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, antiparkinson medicine and the like), antitussive-expectorants (cough and sputum medicines), other cold medicines, antipyretic analgesics, sedatives, or oral medicines containing antihistamines (oral medicines for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicines, anti-allergy medicines). Do not take this medicine if you have stopped taking an MAO inhibitor within the past 2 weeks.
